title: Austin's Big Moves: Offices & Water Bills
summary:
*   City leaders held a work session to discuss the operating budget and capital improvement projects.
*   A public hearing was scheduled for August 14th to discuss a new water conservation rate structure.
*   Plans moved forward to consolidate municipal offices, with city management directed to prepare proposals based on a cost-benefit study.
*   The Mayor requested an alternative plan for the office consolidation that would keep top city offices in the current municipal building.

Water Conservation Rate Structure
The Council, by acclamation, adopted a resolution setting a public hearing on the Water
Conservation Rate Structure for August 14, 1986 at 7:00 p.m.
Consolidation of Municipal Offices
The Council, on Councilmember Carl-Mitchell's motion, Councilmember Rose's second, adopted
a resolution accepting the results of a cost-benefit study of consolidation of certain
municipal offices and directing the City Manager to begin preparation of requests for
proposals. (5-0 Vote, Councilmembers Humphrey and Urdy out of the room.) Councilmember
Cooksey said he would like to see another scenario for the lease, assuming the Mayor and
Council offices; management offices and budget offices remain in the current Municipal
Building. Adjournment The Council adjourned its meeting at 6:00 p.m.
